newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open steady, seen slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open steady, seen slightly firmer.

text.p: Singapore shares opened little changed on Thursday but were expected to firm a little later on the back of demand from overseas funds, dealers said.
"I would think there will continue to be this inflow of foreign buying that we have seen in recent days," said one.
"We should see some of the blue chips recover ground today after the recent profit-taking," said another.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) stood at 2,241.44 points at 0145 GMT, up 1.43. Volume was a healthy 55.9 million shares with 100 gainers and 53 losers.
The most active share was new listing Lung Kee Metal Holdings, which jumped 63 percent from its initial public offer price of US$0.55 to a high of US$0.90 at its debut.
Almost 20 million shares in the stock were traded in the first 45 minutes as stags took profits.
By 0145 GMT, the stock had settled back to around US$0.84.

The top gainer was sound-card maker Creative Technology which continued to benefit from a reevaluation of the prospects for the electronics sector now the recent industry slump has ended. By 0145 GMT, it stood at Singapore $16.70, up 40 cents.
